skill.name: md-context-writer
skill.description: Guide an agent to draft and review CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and scoped rules using repository facts. Referenced automation scripts are not included.
skill.summary: Repository-grounded guidance for concise agent instruction files, with examples for correcting stale commands, paths, and unsafe secret references.
skill.author: nexaiguy

security_audit.summary: All 20 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, attribution links, and an example advising credential removal and rotation. No evidence found of malicious command execution, credential access, exfiltration, reconnaissance, or prompt injection in the supplied guide. Referenced scripts and templates are absent, so their behavior and claimed test coverage cannot be verified.

content.value_statement: Stale agent instructions cause incorrect commands and repeated repository mistakes. This guide helps agents review repository facts and draft concise instructions without claiming unavailable automation.
actual_capabilities: Provides a workflow for grounding instruction files in repository manifests, paths, and CI configuration.
Guides drafting and reviewing CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md with a suggested limit of 200 lines.
Recommends moving area-specific guidance into path-scoped .claude/rules files.
Provides an audit example covering stale commands, removed paths, conflicting rules, and credential exposure.
Directs agents to show a diff and explain removed sections instead of silently dropping content.
limitations: Only SKILL.md is included; referenced scripts, templates, extension source, and automated tests are absent.
Automatic fact collection, linting, and CI enforcement require separately obtained tools whose behavior was not verified here.
The described linter supports selected command runners and checks paths written in backticks, not every possible command or path.
The guide cannot establish whether a repository rule is appropriate; maintainers must review recommendations and tool-specific loading behavior.

use_cases.title: Create Instructions for a New Repository
use_cases.description: Draft concise agent guidance from manifests and CI configuration, marking anything that still requires maintainer confirmation.

use_cases.title: Review Stale Onboarding Guidance
use_cases.description: Compare an existing instruction file with current commands and paths, then review proposed corrections before accepting a diff.

use_cases.title: Organize Monorepo Rules
use_cases.description: Separate shared instructions from area-specific rules and identify where automated drift checks would require additional tooling.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Instruction File
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft CLAUDE.md from this repository's manifests and CI files. Keep it under 200 lines. Mark unverified commands and do not run missing helpers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create an initial instruction file.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Instructions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review AGENTS.md against current repository files. Identify stale commands, missing paths, and conflicting rules. Show a proposed diff with reasons before applying changes.

prompt_templates.title: Separate Scoped Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose splitting this CLAUDE.md into shared instructions and path-scoped .claude/rules files. Verify directory paths and preserve existing intent. Show the complete proposed diff.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: organize instructions across multiple project areas.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Evidence-Based Drift Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit instructions across this monorepo using workspace manifests and CI configuration. Record evidence, flag unverifiable claims, and propose drift checks without assuming missing scripts exist.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: design a repeatable review across workspaces.

output_examples.input: Review an old instruction file containing an obsolete test command, a removed source directory, and an embedded database password.
output: Command review: Flag the obsolete command and propose the current CI command only after confirming it in repository configuration.
Path review: Identify the removed directory and reference a replacement only when repository files support the change.
Secret review: Remove the credential value, retain only the variable name, and recommend rotation without repeating the password.
Validation status: Manual review only; the referenced linter is not included.

output_examples.input: Plan a shorter instruction file for a monorepo with separate frontend and backend conventions.
output: Shared instructions: Keep repository-wide commands and completion checks in the root file.
Scoped rules: Propose separate frontend and backend rules tied to verified directory paths.
Review checkpoint: Present the proposed diff and explain moved or removed sections before applying changes.

best_practices: Ground each command and path in current repository files, and distinguish configured commands from commands actually executed.
Keep shared instructions concise and scope specialized rules to verified paths.
Review the proposed diff and redact secret values; rotate exposed credentials rather than only deleting them from documentation.
anti_patterns: Assuming the referenced scripts, templates, or claimed tests are included in this package.
Copying example commands or paths without checking the target repository.
Embedding credential values or silently deleting maintainer instructions during a rewrite.

faq.question: Does this package include a working linter?
faq.answer: No. It contains only the public guide. The referenced fact collector and linter scripts are not included.

faq.question: Can I use the guide with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes, as documentation guidance. Actual file loading and instruction precedence depend on the target tool and must be checked separately.

faq.question: How does this differ from an initial instruction draft?
faq.answer: It emphasizes repository evidence, reviewing existing instructions, and organizing scoped rules. Continuous automated checks require separate tooling.

faq.question: Will it rewrite my files without approval?
faq.answer: The guide directs the agent to show a diff and explain removals. Your agent's permission settings still control actual file changes.

faq.question: Can it prevent instruction drift in CI?
faq.answer: The guide describes CI linting, but provides no executable implementation. Obtain and review suitable tooling before adding a check.

faq.question: How should exposed credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Remove credential values from instructions, retain variable names when useful, and rotate exposed credentials. Do not reproduce secret values in review output.
